rows.description: After loss or hard reading, prayer feels empty and you question whether anyone listens. Honest doubt is part of many traditions. Ask questions, read widely, talk with thoughtful people, and avoid forcing either belief or disbelief.

related mind states: doubt

rows.description: Angry at God for unfairness or suffering, you may feel guilty for that anger. Many believers have voiced it in prayer and poetry. Say it plainly; anger can be a form of relationship, and no answer is required immediately.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, gratitude, loneliness, rejection, respect, trust
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: anger, guilt

rows.description: Parents expect you to keep every ritual and are hurt by your questions. Speak gently about your inner life, keep respect for their practice, and do not hide or mock. You may share a family ritual while holding your own view.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, contempt, gratitude, loneliness, rejection, respect
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: admiration, hurt

rows.description: People shun or lecture you for doubt or a different path. It hurts as loss of belonging. Seek members who hold questions kindly, keep some connection, and remember that group acceptance is not the measure of your sincerity.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, contempt, gratitude, loneliness, respect, trust
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: doubt, nostalgia, hurt

rows.description: You bring doubts to a teacher, and they respond with patience and honesty rather than fear. Such teachers help faith mature. Listen, question again, and accept that not every question ends in certainty.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, contempt, gratitude, loneliness, rejection, respect
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: fear, doubt, trust

rows.description: You have drifted from belief and miss the comfort of ritual and community. Grief for that loss is real. Find new sources of meaning, such as service, art, reflection or friends, without pretending the old ones did not matter.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, contempt, gratitude, rejection, respect, trust
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: grief, loneliness

rows.description: After recovering from a hard time, you feel deeply thankful, whether or not you have words for it. Let gratitude lead to practical kindness. Faith shows in how you treat others as much as in what you say.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, contempt, loneliness, rejection, respect, trust
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: gratitude

rows.description: A friend with no faith or a different faith asks honest questions. Listen without trying to convert or win, share what your belief means to you, and enjoy the differences. Respect grows from curiosity, not debate.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, contempt, gratitude, loneliness, rejection, trust
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: admiration, curiosity

rows.description: Someone mocks your faith as foolish. It stings and tempts you to argue or hit back. Answer briefly, without defensiveness, set limits on jokes, and remember that their dismissal says more about them than your worth.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, gratitude, loneliness, rejection, respect, trust
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: contempt

rows.description: Their teachings give calm and purpose and you feel grateful. Keep devotion healthy: ask questions, keep your job, family and money in your own hands, and watch that love for the teacher does not replace your judgment.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, coercion, disillusionment, exploitation, fear, protectiveness
